arxiv-2111-11050.title: (P)reheating Effects of the Kähler Moduli Inflation I Model
arxiv-2111-11050.creator: Islam Khan, Aaron C. Vincent, Guy Worthey
arxiv-2111-11050.description: Abstract We investigate reheating in the string-theory-motivated Kähler Moduli Inflation I (KMII) potential, coupled to a light scalar field χ \chi and produce constraints and forecasts based on Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and gravitational wave observables. We implement a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling method to compute the adopted model’s parameter ranges allowed by the current CMB observations.

arxiv-2502-01860.title: SE Arena: An Interactive Platform for Evaluating Foundation Models in Software Engineering
arxiv-2502-01860.creator: Zhimin Zhao
arxiv-2502-01860.description: Abstract Foundation models (FMs), particularly large language models (LLMs), have shown significant promise in various software engineering (SE) tasks, including code generation, debugging, and requirement refinement. Despite these advances, existing evaluation frameworks are insufficient for assessing model performance in iterative, context-rich workflows characteristic of SE activities.

pmc-10674678.title: Humoral and Cellular Immunity Are Significantly Affected in Renal Transplant Recipients, following Vaccination with BNT162b2
pmc-10674678.creator: Asimina Fylaktou, Stamatia Stai, Efstratios Kasimatis, Aliki Xochelli, Vasiliki Nikolaidou, Anastasia Papadopoulou, Grigorios Myserlis, Georgios Lioulios, Despoina Asouchidou, Maria Giannaki, Evangelia Yannaki, Georgios Tsoulfas, Aikaterini Papagianni, Maria Stangou
pmc-10674678.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Renal transplant recipients (RTRs) tend to mount weaker immune responses to vaccinations, including vaccines against the novel severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Humoral immunity was assessed using anti-receptor binding domain (RBD) and neutralizing antibodies (NAb) serum levels measured by ELISA, and cellular immunity was assessed using T-, B-, NK, natural killer-like T (NKT)-cell subpopulations, and monocytes measured by flow cytometry, and also specific T-cell immunity, at predefined time points after BNT162b2 vaccination, in 57 adult RTRs.

pmc-12541981.title: Association between hot spring residency and dry eye disease: a crossover gene–environment interaction (GxE) study in Taiwan
pmc-12541981.creator: Hsin-Yu Wu, Kao-Jung Chang, Wei Chiu, Ching-Yun Wang, Yi-Chen Lin, Yu-Tien Hsu, Yuan-Chih Wen, Pin-Hsuan Chiang, Yu-Hsiang Chen, He-Jhen Dai, Chia-Hsin Lu, Yi-Cheng Chen, Han-Ying Tsai, Yu-Chun Chen, Chih-Hung Hsu, Shih-Hwa Chiou, Yi-Ping Yang, Ai-Ru Hsieh, Chih-Chien Hsu
pmc-12541981.description: Background/aimsThe advent of genetic biobanking has powered gene-environment interaction (GxE) studies in various disease contexts. Therefore, we aimed to discover novel GxE effects that address hot spring residency as a risk to inconspicuous disease association.MethodsA complete genetic and demographic registry comprising 129,451 individuals was obtained from Taiwan Biobank (TWB).

pmc-12566685.title: Inclusive Nutrition Care for LGBT+ Patients: Challenges and Opportunities for Dietitians—A Narrative Review
pmc-12566685.creator: Michał Czapla, Anthony Dissen
pmc-12566685.description: Nutrition is a cornerstone of public health, yet the unique nutrition needs and considerations of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and others (LGBT+) communities remain largely invisible in the field of dietetics. These populations face disproportionate burdens of obesity, eating disorders, body dysmorphia, metabolic risks, and food insecurity, often driven by stigma, minority stress, and structural inequities.

pmc-13030363.title: Vaccine-Induced Immune Thrombotic Thrombocytopenia (VITT): An Immunopathogenic Model of Dysregulated Vaccine-Triggered Immunity
pmc-13030363.creator: Carmine Siniscalchi, Manuela Basaglia, Antonella Tufano, Egidio Imbalzano, Pierpaolo Di Micco
pmc-13030363.description: Background/Objectives: Vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) is a rare but severe immune-mediated adverse event associated with adenoviral vector-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccines. Beyond its clinical relevance, VITT provides a unique human model of vaccine-triggered autoimmunity and immune-thrombosis. This review critically reassesses the immunopathogenic framework of VITT in light of recent evidence.

pmc-13341151.title: Herbivore Identity and Species Richness Shape Fruit Chemical and Quality Responses to Foliar Herbivory
pmc-13341151.creator: Xavier Ozowara, Taylor M Sloey, Susan R Whitehead
pmc-13341151.description: The cascading consequences of foliar herbivory on fruit chemistry and quality remain relatively underexplored, with most existing studies focusing on the effects of only one or two attackers. In this study, we examine how increasing herbivore species richness during foliar herbivory alters strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch) fruit quality and phenolic chemistry.
